one sees the path of the gods (<s>devayāna</s>) in the solar disc.
And the <s>Vaiśvānarī</s> knowledge shines forth in one's own body;
having practiced the <s>Haviṣpāntīya</s>, one is freed from all sins.
'<s>Indraṃ stava</s>' (Praise <s>Indra</s>)—this hymn one should recite for the destruction of enemies;
the most purifying of purifiers, secret, cleansing, wondrous.
In the bright fortnight, on an auspicious day, under a good constellation and good planetary position,
on the twelfth [lunar day], one should prepare a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> <s>caru</s> (oblation) for one desiring a son.
The couple should fast on the eleventh [day] at a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
having duly worshipped <s>Janārdana</s> with sixteen <s>Ṛg</s> verses,
one should cook the <s>caru</s> with the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>, desiring a son;
one obtains a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> son before long, capable of continuing the lineage.
One who properly prepares the <s>caru</s> with milk on twelve <s>dvādaśīs</s> (twelfth lunar days)—
there would be a thousand [blessings]; he goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having duly offered in the fire according to rules, with sixteen <s>Ṛg</s> verses, the wise one,
having formed the <s>añjali</s> (joined palms), should employ the praise with those [verses].
[One should worship] <s>Keśava</s> in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>; in <s>Pauṣa</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is remembered;
<s>Mādhava</s> in the month of <s>Māgha</s>; and <s>Govinda</s> in <s>Phālguna</s> likewise.
In <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>; in <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>Madhusūdana</s>;
in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, one should know <s>Trivikrama</s>; in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, they know <s>Vāmana</s>.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, one should know <s>Śrīdhara</s>; <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> in the next [month];
in <s>Āśvina</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>; and <s>Dāmodara</s> in <s>Kārttika</s>.
These twelve names the sage <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> declared;
worshipping with the monthly names, one obtains all wishes.
One begets a long-lived son, endowed with fame and intelligence,
wealthy, having progeny, righteous, and of <s>sāttvika</s> (pure) nature.
Having offered firewood of the <s>Aśvattha</s> (sacred fig) tree in the fire, one should offer again;
worship of the sacred fire, meditating on and worshipping <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
Then one should perform the oblation verse by verse, with restrained speech, pure;
one should offer ghee with the hymn at the beginning and end, as before.
Having bowed to the food-remnant, the woman [should bow to] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, [her] husband;
having eaten the food-remnant, having received blessings, she should retire for the night.
Then, having done this rite, the offering of water to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>dvijatarpaṇa</s>) should be performed;
[the husband] should retire with the wife until she conceives.
One who is childless, or whose children have died, or who gives birth to daughters only—
she quickly begets a son, as <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> declared.
I shall now describe the worship (<s>arcā</s>) of <s>Viṣṇu</s> of immeasurable splendor,
by doing which all sages attain <s>Brahma-nirvāṇa</s> (liberation in <s>Brahman</s>).
In water, in fire, in the heart, in the sun, on a platform (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>), and in images—
in these six, the proper worship of <s>Hari</s> is remembered by the sages.
In fire is the God for those who perform rituals; in heaven is the God for the wise;
in images for those of limited understanding; for <s>yogins</s>, <s>Hari</s> is in the heart.
Water is His abode; therefore <s>Hari</s> is always in the waters;
and because of His all-pervasiveness, [He is worshipped] on a platform by those of purified minds.
He who offers flowers or even water with the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>—
by him this entire world, moving and unmoving, is worshipped.
Of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> hymn ending in <s>Triṣṭubh</s>, the deity
is <s>Puruṣa</s>, the seed of the universe; the seer is remembered as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
'O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, mighty-armed one, listen with one-pointed mind, O Lord;
I shall declare the prescribed method of worship through the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>.
The fire-rite, the method of recitation, and the praise that is ever pure—
having bathed according to the prescribed rules, facing east, with purified mind,
one should place the first [verse] on the left hand, the second on the right hand;
the third on the left foot, the fourth on the right foot.
The fifth on the left knee, the sixth on the right knee;
the seventh on the left hip, the eighth on the right hip.
The ninth in the middle of the navel, the tenth on the heart;
the eleventh in the region of the throat, the twelfth on the left arm.
The thirteenth on the right [arm], the fourteenth on the mouth;
the fifteenth on the eyes, and the sixteenth on the crown of the head.
Having thus performed the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) procedure, afterwards one should commence the worship;
as on the body, so on the deity, having performed <s>nyāsa</s> according to the rules.
With the first [verse], one should invoke (<s>āvāhana</s>) the god, the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>;
with the second, one should offer a seat (<s>āsana</s>); and with the third, water for washing the feet (<s>pādya</s>).
Ceremonial water (<s>arghya</s>) should be given with the fourth; with the fifth, water for sipping (<s>ācamanīya</s>);
with the sixth, one should perform the bathing (<s>snāna</s>); and with the seventh, [offer] a garment.
With the eighth, the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>); with the ninth, anointing paste (<s>anulepa</s>);
flowers should be given with the tenth; with the eleventh, incense (<s>dhūpa</s>).
With the twelfth, one should give a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>); with the thirteenth, food-offering (<s>nivedana</s>);
with the fourteenth, obeisance (<s>namaskāra</s>); with the fifteenth, circumambulation (<s>pradakṣiṇa</s>).
At bathing, garments, and food-offering, one should give water for sipping;
and according to one's ability, a gift (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) should be given with the sixteenth [verse].
Then, having performed circumambulation, one should recite with concentration;
having recited according to one's ability, one should dedicate the hymn to the deity.
On the right side of the deity, one should construct a fire-pit (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) or platform (<s>sthaṇḍila</s>);
with the first [verse], [the pit is prepared]; with the second, sprinkling (<s>prokṣaṇa</s>).
With the third, one should establish the fire; with the fourth, kindling;
with the fifth, heating the ghee, and likewise cooking the <s>caru</s> (oblation).
With the sixth, in the middle of the fire, one should visualize a lotus seat;
one should meditate on the Lord of gods, resplendent like the fire of dissolution (<s>kālānala</s>).
Then sandalwood paste, flowers, incense, lamp, and food-offering—
having taken permission, one should then perform [the offerings] with the seventh onwards, in order.
One should first offer that many fuel-sticks (<s>samidh</s>), consecrated;
then one should offer with ghee, and then again with the <s>caru</s>.
Having thus offered and then taken permission in due order,
near the fire of the Lord, one should recite the hymn of praise (<s>stotra</s>):
'Victory to you, O lotus-eyed one (<s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>)! Obeisance to you, O creator of the universe (<s>Viśvabhāvana</s>)!
Obeisance to you, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (lord of the senses), O <s>Mahāpuruṣa</s>, the first-born!
Common supreme deity of both gods and demons,
I always take refuge at the pair of your feet.
You alone are the creator and also the destroyer of the world,
the unmanifest, the approver, enveloped in the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).
The terrible, endless ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (transmigration), the receptacle of afflictions—
the wise, having reached you alone as refuge, cross over it.
You have no form, no shape, no weapons, and no abode;
yet, O <s>Puruṣa</s>-formed one, you manifest yourself to your devotees.
Nothing whatsoever is hidden from you, yet you are not perceptible to anyone;
nothing whatsoever is impossible for you, yet you are not attainable by anyone.
The first cause of effects, the supreme [goal] of words,
the highest attainment of <s>yogins</s>—they know it as your supreme abode.
I am afraid, O Lord of gods, in this <s>saṃsāra</s> of great fear;
save me, O lotus-eyed one—I do not know the supreme abode.
In all times and in all directions, O <s>Acyuta</s> (the imperishable one),
though you have entered the body, I have great fear.
Other than your lotus feet, I [have] nothing, even in other births;
this knowledge that I have gained, this station that I have attained—
even in another birth, O Lord, let there be no loss of this;
even if I must be born in a lowly state, may my mind's aspiration be directed toward you.
If it does not perish, by that much I am always fulfilled;
I desire only the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s> in all births.'
The <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s> of <s>Hari</s> is heavenly, bestowing wealth and fame;
this is the sacred knowledge of the Self (<s>ātmajñāna</s>), this is the supreme knowledge of <s>yoga</s>.
One who lives on fruits for a month sees the Self in the Self;
having eaten fruits, one should fast for a month and subsist on water alone.
One should always dwell in the forest, reciting this seer constantly;
three times, at the three <s>savana</s>-times (dawn, noon, sunset), one should bathe in water, concentrated.
One should worship the sun always with this hymn;
having offered ghee oblations with this, one should meditate on this seer.
After a month of fruit-diet, within three years one conquers heaven;
devoted to that, with mind fixed on that, for ten years, with undivided attention,
one directly sees that God, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the disease-free;
one should grasp with utmost effort the imperishable creator of the universe.
Abiding in the householder's <s>dharma</s>, lawfully established, with pure vows,
one should meditate on this God, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the disease-free.
At midnight, having abandoned sleep, rising, pure, with restrained speech,
when beings are sound asleep, the knower of <s>yoga</s> should practice <s>yoga</s>.
Sitting upright in a level place, sheltered from wind, free from noise,
one should then press the left foot against the right knee.
Drawing back the right foot, one places it on the left knee;
having formed the <s>brahmāñjali</s> (gesture of Brahman), steady, with eyes closed in <s>yoga</s>.
Having uttered <s>Om</s>, one should contemplate one's own heart, without hesitation;
there one should fix the Self, and the senses, and the mind likewise.
If one perceives nothing else, neither sees nor hears anything,
and does not think—then one is said to have attained <s>yoga</s>.
One should practice this seer in the heart, as if seeing [him] according to scripture;
having restrained the breaths (<s>prāṇāyāma</s>), seated, one should contemplate that seer as long [as possible].
About to exhale, having brought the mind down below the navel,
one should exhale; thus repeatedly, with mind absorbed, one should elevate the <s>yoga</s>.
Thus practicing equally, when one neither sees nor hears,
then one should gradually raise the consciousness from the heart upwards.
The collarbones, mouth, nose, eyes, and eyebrows are equal [stations];
between the eyebrows is the supreme station—there one should hold [the consciousness] firmly.
Having held [it] in the forehead region, then one should move it to the crown of the head;
and exhaling at the proper time, having gone to the navel, one should exhale again.
This is declared as the supreme station of <s>Brahman</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>);
the great soul, thus united [in <s>yoga</s>], attains the Self.
Whether one is of good deeds and pure, or even the worst sinner,
having apprehended the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> and known the way, one becomes pure.
If one is beset by all sins, knowing this and being prepared, one should recite;
even merely by the desire to know, one attains the supreme goal.
<s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) should be practiced separately, constantly through this <s>dharma</s>;
one should concentrate on the sun, fire, the moon, and treetops.
On a mountain peak, in the ocean, or wherever the mind delights;
but upon reaching sense-objects, one should never practice concentration.
One should know that there is much suffering when concentration is disrupted;
one who has fallen from <s>yoga</s> is born in a pure family of righteous people.
When one finds <s>Brahman</s> at the crown of the head, [one becomes] that best of <s>ṛṣis</s>;
then one should raise the supreme light from the crown to the path of the stars.
The <s>yogī</s>, having attained the Lord of <s>yoga</s>, free from dualities, the supreme knower of the Self,
should see the Self everywhere by the Self alone, devoted to the <s>ṛṣi</s> [tradition].
One should always recite this supreme purification after bathing;
even one joined with sin becomes meritorious in time.
Devoted to austerity always, truthful in speech, free from envy—
a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> reciting this <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn], in time becomes a forest-dweller (<s>vanī</s>).
With whatever desire one always recites this <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn],
that desire is fulfilled for one who acts with faith.
Whether <s>homa</s> (oblation), or recitation, or offering, or <s>caru</s> (cooked oblation)—
whatever desire one performs [these] with, one should be certain of its success.
Pre-eminence among kinsmen, great wealth, fame in the world, the supreme goal,
and liberation from sin—one should be certain of its success.
That which is attainable through knowledge, supreme, subtle, pervading all and established everywhere,
grasped by utmost effort—one approaches the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.
The hymn '<s>sahasra-śīrṣā</s>' (Thousand-headed [<s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>]) grants the fruits of all desires;
he whose body contains the <s>Vedas</s> is known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indu</s> (Soma), <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Parjanya</s> are established in this hymn;
in this [hymn] should be seen this world, both the stationary and the moving.
Even when unable to approach [him], one should not neglect devotion;
the Lord <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person) is heard to be compassionate toward devotees.
For the worship of that god, with forest [products] self-gathered,
one should offer <s>caru</s> daily according to the <s>Āraṇyaka</s> procedure,
[saying] '<s>Nārāyaṇāya svāhā</s>' at the end of the mantra, one should offer the oblation.
After a thousand [oblations], the fire grants divine vision to the offerer;
or, one may offer a thousand <s>caru</s> in a single session.
Or however many are possible, one should complete them all in a day;
one obtains the fruits of a thousand desired wishes.
Endowed with a full human lifespan, or even perfected, one may wander the earth.
One should always meditate upon <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, dwelling in the middle of the solar orb, seated upon a lotus throne,
wearing armlets and <s>makara</s>-shaped earrings, crowned, wearing garlands, with a golden body, bearing the conch and discus.
He who recites this hymn alone, having bowed to the venerable feet of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>—
by that supreme recitation, he attains the abode of the eternal <s>Viṣṇu</s>, free from old age and death.
With oblations in the fire, flowers in water, through meditation upon <s>Hari</s> in the heart—
the wise ones always worship with recitation in the solar orb.
<s>Bilva</s> leaf, <s>śamī</s> leaf, <s>bhṛṅgāraka</s> leaf, <s>mālatī</s>, <s>kuśa</s>, and lotus—
these immediately please <s>Hari</s>.
Whatever is not available, one should meditate upon it with the mind alone;
it comes about by the grace of the god of gods, the discus-bearer (<s>Cakrin</s>).
With leaves and flowers and water, obtained without purchase, always among the righteous—
for the primeval <s>Puruṣa</s>, obtainable through devotion alone, why is no effort made for liberation?
Thus has been stated the mode of worship of <s>Puruṣa Viṣṇu</s>, [composed] by one named <s>Viṣṇukumāra</s>,
for the purpose of awakening to the sole path to liberation, having seen the prescriptions stated here by <s>Nārada</s>.
One who recites '<s>yā oṣadhīḥ</s>' as a benediction, observing a constant vow—
one should conquer [disease through] herbs, always, for six months continually.
Having worshipped <s>Rudra</s> in autumn and likewise herbs,
one's diseases do not occur, and those already present are also healed.
The rite should be performed seven times over seven nights; then
the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should approach the herb, always reciting this hymn.
[Saying] 'come here from the enemy's field'—one should thus entreat;
having worshipped <s>Varuṇa</s> in one's own field, one obtains the herbs from the enemy.
One desiring rain, with controlled food, should approach <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
accompanied by a milk-pudding offering and oblation.
[The hymn] '<s>Bṛhaspate pati</s>'—one desiring rain should employ this;
having paid homage to <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god), one obtains beautiful rainfall.
This invincible <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn] should be known as [granting] supreme peace in all [situations];
whatever country one goes to, or even [against] an enemy, being thus consecrated—
one does not return without conquering, for the power of <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) is supreme.
With all desires, one should recite this for the fulfillment of all desires.
This should be employed for a king setting out for battle;
he conquers all enemies and is not conquered by others.
This is a benediction on the road; while traveling, [it protects] from robbers,
spirits, serpents, <s>piśācas</s>—it protects from all.
One desiring progeny, being pure, should recite the <s>Bhūtāṃśa Kāśyapa</s> hymn;
one quickly obtains offspring of similar kind—there is no doubt.
A twice-born should worship the <s>Aśvins</s> (<s>Nāsatyas</s>) with <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering);
with this very hymn, having offered oblations, one should consecrate horses.
Milk-pudding, <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-sesame dish), meat, cooked rice, yogurt, barley flour,
<s>kulmāṣa</s> (cooked pulses), <s>karambha</s> (parched grain), and various fruits—
varied [foods], maternal [offerings], fine perfumes, and whatever food and drink,
eatables, foods, and drinks—having assembled [these] at sunrise—
one should practice the <s>Bhūtāṃśa</s> [hymn] until sunset;
after midnight has passed, one should then offer [the food] to the <s>Aśvins</s>.
One obtains a son who is long-lived, handsome, and of great splendor;
one who always practices the <s>Bhūtāṃśa</s> [hymn] becomes handsome always.
The discerning person should know this <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn] as fulfilling all desires (<s>sārvakāmika</s>).
One observing a fixed vow should recite '<s>na vā u devāḥ</s>.'
One finds food everywhere, wherever one stays.
He who is discerning and considers himself afflicted by sin—
he, having become restrained, should recite [this]; he considers [himself] light from sin.
One desiring speech should approach <s>Vāc</s> (Speech), offering and quickly reciting these [verses].
'<s>Aham rudrebhiḥ</s>'—[by reciting] this, one becomes eloquent and honored.
The wise one reciting the eight-versed <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> hymn '<s>natam</s>'—
having destroyed all sin, sits together with the <s>Viśve Devas</s>.
One should always approach <s>Rātri</s> (Night), pure, with completed vows, at night.
He who desires 'may I not be born again in wombs'—
should recite a thousand times mentally '<s>Rātri</s>' during the nights.
With <s>sthālīpāka</s> one should worship <s>Rātri</s> every day at night;
with mind absorbed at night one should sit; during the day one should stand, being righteous.
After a year, with <s>caru</s> prepared in milk,
a thousand-fold <s>homa</s> is prescribed by day with this [verse].
One should offer at night in the first part [of the night], absorbed in <s>Rātri</s>;
and during the day, the necessary [rites] should be performed in the shade, by the sun's rays.
Thus, with controlled self, one should recite the hymn mentally;
in the third year, one should prepare <s>caru</s> with ghee.
Then the goddess <s>Rātri</s>, the night, becomes a boon-granting deity;
one entreats that goddess, the boon-giver, who has come of her own accord.
'In this year, in this season, in this month, on this day, even at this moment,
the time for your departure will come, my child'—so speaks the loving [goddess].
Reciting the <s>Rātri Sūkta</s>, one attains that time [of death];
one does not return to a womb and is freed from all sins.
'<s>Mama agne varcaḥ</s>'—a twice-born should recite this with all desires;
offering ghee with this very [verse], one obtains all desires.
'<s>Yām kalpayanti</s>'—one observing a fixed vow should always recite [this];
sorceries (<s>kṛtyā</s>) do not harm him, nor spells cast in anger.
Whoever is bewitched by those who know the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> spells—
by the <s>Pratyaṅgirasa</s> (counter-<s>Āṅgirasa</s>) procedure, he repels all of them.
One who knows <s>Pratyaṅgirasa</s> is never harmed;
sorceries do not harm him, whether known or unknown.
Whether by one unknowing or knowing, by one angry or impatient—
abuse or harsh speech does not stain the one who knows this.
Thus one should always recite this <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn] for one's own welfare;
the <s>ṛṣi</s> himself declared this as the universal expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>).
At the establishing of permanent [settlements], cities,
villages, and houses, one should always recite this <s>ṛṣi</s> [hymn].
A wise person should make a golden triply-wound amulet;
having offered a thousand oblations with this <s>ṛṣi</s>—
one should bind it on the head, or on the neck, or on the chest;
sorceries do not harm him, whether known or unknown.
With this very hymn, a wise person should make an amulet mixed with copper for kings;
the consecration is the same.
In battles, one should consecrate the tops of banners, musical instruments,
seats, beds, and various vehicles.
When the <s>Āṅgirasa</s> <s>ṛṣi</s> himself directly performs sorcery,
by the <s>Pratyaṅgirasa</s> procedure, all of that is repelled.
Against non-human beings, reciting this sorcery-hymn,
one is freed from all adversities—how much more then from human fear?
If the practitioner be an ascetic, restrained, self-controlled <s>ṛṣi</s>,
he crosses over everything, with a pacified self—for austerity (<s>tapas</s>) is a supremely great power.
The great <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s> hymn, [granting] life, longevity, and splendor—
having obtained an ornament or gold, one should recite the <s>Dākṣāyaṇa</s>.
One takes on attained prosperity and enjoys abundant food.
One should recite '<s>na asad āsīt</s>' (<s>Nāsadīya</s> hymn) and offer [oblations], devoted to <s>yoga</s>;
one attains union (<s>sāyojya</s>) with <s>Prajāpati</s> in twelve years.
One who is ill, observing a controlled vow, should recite '<s>uta devāḥ</s>';
having placed a pot of ghee, one should offer [it] in the fire of <s>Jātavedas</s>;
from the pot, one should place the overflow into another bronze vessel.
He who is fit for food but has no food should prepare this;
having anointed the body with that ghee, one gradually becomes a partaker of food.
For one afflicted by disease also, having anointed the body with this very [ghee] and reciting this—
even for indigestion, one should anoint—comfort comes from that.
'<s>Agne acchā vada</s>'—one desiring wealth should employ this;
being restrained, having offered ghee with this, one should recite ten thousand times again.
One should offer a hundred sets of ten <s>khadira</s>-wood sticks;
performing ten times, with wife, one prospers with increasing wealth.
<s>Bilva</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, and also <s>rohītaka</s> [woods]—
one desiring wealth should offer them; one prospers with increasing wealth.
With <s>vibhītaka</s> fuel, one should offer <s>bilva</s> [offerings] while eating half-meals;
at the end, with hatred toward the enemy, one should employ this hymn.
Having destroyed a wealthy enemy, one obtains the enemy's wealth;
or, recitation alone is prescribed for one desiring wealth and increasing prosperity.
'<s>Ayam agne jaritā</s>'—one should recite when there is danger from fire.
having satisfied the fire according to the prescribed method with milk, yogurt, ghee, and the like.
He himself should go in the four directions as far as he wishes to drink [the herb];
he should bring [this herb to] water with a continuous stream of water.
Becoming like a pool of water, [this is] the medicine for fire [disease] nearby.
Having gone to the forest, one should purchase the <s>pāṭhā</s> herb with a handful of barley:
'If you are of <s>Soma</s>'s [nature], I purchase you as a medicine for <s>Soma</s>;
if you are of <s>Varuṇa</s>'s [nature], I purchase you then for <s>Varuṇa</s>.'
'Or for the <s>Vasus</s>, or for the <s>Rudras</s>, or again for the <s>Ādityas</s>;
if you belong to all the gods (<s>Vaiśvadevī</s>), I purchase you then for the <s>Viśvedevas</s>.'
Having first cast flowers, together with the herb and the plant,
one absorbs its potency — for the rite where it will be employed.
One should place that [herb] in the open air among other herbs.
In the gathering of herbs, this procedure should apply everywhere.
One should uproot that <s>pāṭhā</s> herb, reciting '<s>imām</s>' here;
and in the morning, it should be ground in an assembly by a <s>brahmacārin</s>.
In the absence of such [a person], by one observing vows, a maiden, or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;
in the morning, purified, one should drink it three times with ghee, [the herb] having been consecrated [with mantras].
With the hymn '<s>imām</s>', a hundred times, with a minimum of ten —
by that, one subdues a co-wife, and the husband regards [one] very highly.
The husband, having recited [the mantra] over this <s>pāṭhā</s> herb, should drink it with this [hymn],
with milk for seven nights — he repels rival co-wives.
A woman who wishes to conquer her husband through recitations of other root-mantras,
worldless, dwelling in the realm of <s>Yama</s>, she sinks into hell indeed.
And powders, roots, and medicines brought by other [methods]
would destroy the man — therefore one should not practice anything else.
A woman who speaks lovingly to her husband, for whom the husband is the supreme refuge,
whose speech is sweet — [that itself] is the greatest subjugation of the husband.
Having obtained a dear husband, one should indeed drink this herb;
a sweet-speaking woman, devoted to <s>dharma</s>, a <s>dharma</s>-wife, blameless —
one who foolishly disrespects [such a wife] is called the lowest of men.
'<s>Araṇyānī</s>' — in forests, one should recite this hymn many times;
having paid obeisance to <s>Araṇyānī</s> (the forest goddess), one is freed from the forest [dangers].
One desiring faith should always recite the faith-hymn (<s>śraddhāsūkta</s>), concentrated;
one obtains faith everywhere. Likewise the intellect-hymn (<s>medhāsūkta</s>).
Having obtained the <s>brāhmī</s> [herb], one should recite both hymns, observing the vow with discipline;
one should drink it according to one's capacity — within three days, one attains success.
<s>Śaṅkhapuṣpī</s> with milk; <s>brāhmī</s> flowers with ghee;
<s>Śatāvarī</s> with milk; <s>varcā</s> with water or ghee —
having consecrated each with these two hymns, one should drink one [herb] for three days each.
One obtains faith, intellect, memory, nourishment, strength, and prosperity;
and one attains supreme accomplishment and enjoys long life.
Or one may simply meditate mentally [on the hymns] — one attains success.
'<s>Śām itthā</s>' — [the hymn that is] enemy-destroying, for one wishing to conquer in battle,
should be employed by one who is pure; one should offer [oblations] for its success.
Or it may simply be recited by one going into battle.
'<s>Śām itthā</s>' — by which one who [wishes to] slay would ward off all enemies.
For the destruction of misfortune, one should always recite the <s>Śirimbiṭa</s> [hymn].
Taking a branch of <s>apāmārga</s> (Achyranthes aspera), together with <s>darbha</s> grass and herbs,
one should purify oneself [by passing it] downward and upward, daily.
And one should offer ghee with this, a thousand [times] — ten times ten;
within three days, one removes from the body misfortune of a hundred years' standing.
One performing the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (moon-penance) vow should recite this success-granting hymn;
one removes from the body misfortune even of a thousand years' standing.
One seized by consumption (<s>yakṣma</s>), taking <s>darbha</s> grass and touching [the patient], should recite;
'<s>muñcāmi tvā haviṣā</s>' (I release you with an offering) — it draws out the consumption.
One should offer [oblations] into the kindled fire with ghee according to the prescribed method;
one should pour the remnants into the ghee, and with the remnants drink milk.
In the remnant-vessel, one should place ghee and powder;
there his food and drink should be [prepared,] consecrated with mantras.
And <s>khadira</s> (Acacia catechu) wood, having made into powder together with water,
one should purify the extract and drink it together with honey and ghee.
'<s>Muñcāmi tvā haviṣā</s>' — this should be employed in each [procedure];
they draw out the consumption from the body through that rite.
When a woman's embryo perishes, one should offer oblations into the fire:
'<s>brahmaṇā agniḥ saṃvidānaḥ</s>' — with ghee, according to the prescribed method.
Having anointed the pregnant woman with the ghee-remnant, she then gives birth;
she should indeed drink the ghee-remnant — a living [child] is born to her.
If those already born should die, having made ghee consecrated with mantras,
one should offer with '<s>brahmaṇā agniḥ</s>' and pour the remnants onto an amulet.
The amulet should be wrapped in a three-stranded thread together with a cloth,
with a shoot of the <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) tree, wrapped in white and red [cloth].
That [amulet] should be consecrated with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (Gāyatrī) ten thousand times, according to the prescribed method,
and with ten thousand remnant-offerings, praised with '<s>brahmaṇā</s>';
and on top, with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the same number of consecrations;
one should recite all the <s>svastyayana</s> (auspiciousness hymns) over the fire-consecrated amulet.
The woman, purified and pregnant, should wear it on her head;
in the third month of pregnancy, she should take up this amulet.
The woman in her season, for [the duration of] a year — like a cow with her calf,
with abundant water and pasture, together with the suckling calf.
When the boy is born, one should fasten the amulet on his neck;
placing the ghee-remnant first, having anointed the boy [with it],
having offered with the <s>svastyayana</s> hymns alone — the woman gives birth to a male child.
After a year, the <s>svastyayana</s> is prescribed again.
Before giving the breast, one should feed him with the <s>śraddhā</s>-hymn (faith-hymn);
and with the <s>medhā</s>-hymn (intellect-hymn), [one should feed him] a rice-cake made of ground rice,
mixed with honey and gold — thereby one of keen intellect is born;
one lives a hundred years and does not die before [the natural span of] life.
Memory indeed becomes established for him, from the sixth month onward.
Having prepared ghee [with mantras], the <s>dvija</s> should offer with '<s>akṣibhyām te</s>';
then with a hand smeared with ghee, one should touch the head,
the ears, the eyes, the chin, and the nostrils — one should touch [all of these].
Reciting this always in this manner, one is freed from consumption.
By the previously described procedure, one should perform the cure for consumption.
Through oblations and recitations, one should perform the cure for consumption.
One should also recite the hymn '<s>apehi</s>', purified — it destroys bad dreams.
'<s>Devāḥ kapota</s>' — when a pigeon alights [on one's house],
one should offer ghee with [this] hymn — for they know it [the pigeon] to be a messenger of <s>Yama</s>.
One should employ the <s>ṛṣabha</s> (bull [hymn]) as enemy-destroying, in recitation and oblation;
'<s>Yena idam</s>' — one should always recite this, observing the vow with discipline;
through that one obtains mental concentration and is never deluded.
'<s>Mayo bhūr vāta</s>' — one should recite this as a <s>svastyayana</s> for cattle.
Barley smeared with ghee, into a fire of cow-dung, concentrated,
one should offer in the middle of the cow-pen, [barley] prepared with yogurt, honey, and ghee.
One should consecrate a king [with the <s>abhiṣeka</s> rite] under the asterism <s>Tiṣya</s> (Puṣya) or <s>Śravaṇa</s>,
or under <s>Pauṣṇa</s> (Revatī), <s>Sāvitra</s> (Hasta), <s>Saumya</s> (Mṛgaśīrṣa), <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, or the <s>Uttarās</s> (Uttarā Phālgunī/Uttarā Āṣāḍhā/Uttarā Bhādrapadā).
Having offered to the fire with the verses pertaining to royalty, and with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, purified and disciplined,
and with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances), [the rite] should be consecrated with remnant-offerings.
With the smooth juices of all herbs and with the waters of rivers,
having seated [the king] on a tiger-skin upon a throne, and having anointed him,
standing facing west, one should say: 'May you conquer this earth!
O King, may your entire <s>dharma</s> increase as you protect the people!'
'May you prosper for glory, nourishment, victory, and prosperity!
May there be kings in your lineage!' Then one should recite the '<s>apratiratham</s>' (invincible [hymn]).
The skin should be of tiger; the firewood should be of <s>audumbara</s> (fig-tree).
Having anointed him thus, one should consecrate the drums [with mantras]:
'In the eastern direction, may the <s>Vasus</s> anoint you for splendor!'
'In the southern direction, may the <s>Rudras</s> anoint you for growth!'
'In the western direction, may the <s>Ādityas</s> anoint you for nourishment!'
'In the northern direction, may the <s>Viśvedevas</s> anoint you for well-being!'
Having anointed the king and congratulated him with blessings,
one should then consecrate him with '<s>ā tvā ahārṣam antaredhī</s>'.
One should always recite '<s>pataṅgam</s>' — it destroys ignorance;
this indeed destroys <s>māyā</s> (illusion) — it repels all <s>māyās</s>.
One should ward off <s>Śāmbarī</s> [magic], <s>Indrajāla</s> (magical web), or [any] <s>māyā</s> with this;
it repels the <s>māyā</s> of unseen beings with this.
'<s>Tyam ūṣu</s>' — one should recite as a <s>svastyayana</s>, observing the vow with discipline.
A woman of age who, having seen her menses, does not conceive —
'<s>Viṣṇur yonim</s>' — touching the womb, one should then recite this.
'<s>Mahi trīṇām avo astv</s>' — one should recite this as a <s>svastyayana</s> on the road.
'<s>Pra Agnaye</s>' — against a hateful enemy, one should recite this as the expiation of enmity.
'<s>Āyam gauḥ</s>' and the <s>Sārparājñī</s> [hymns] — with this, one repels all [snakes and dangers].
The purest of purifiers — one should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> (sin-destroying hymn);
one who, having entered the waters, recites this three times with full concentration —
it is like the concluding bath of the <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse-sacrifice) — so declared <s>Manu</s>.
Just as the <s>Aśvamedha</s>, king of rites, drives away all sins,
so too the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> hymn drives away all sins.
This is the army-scatterer; '<s>nairhastya</s>' [is another designation], says <s>Śaunaka</s>.
This should be meditated upon mentally — so thinks the sage <s>Śaunaka</s>.
'<s>Sam samid yuvase vṛṣan</s>' — [this is] the great [hymn] for creating brotherhood.
One should employ it when kinsmen are divided — they are never divided again.
When division has occurred, one should recite this peace-making [hymn] for reconciliation;
division does not arise again where this is constantly recited.
'<s>Tac chamyor ā vṛṇīmahe</s>' — one should recite this as a <s>svastyayana</s>.
The <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> (Great Names) are the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the bright, eternal light;
they destroy enemies, are auspicious — the <s>Pāvamānīs</s> (purificatory hymns) are declared supreme.
One desiring rain should recite these: '<s>Āpo hi ṣṭhāḥ</s>' — the eternal [hymns],
preceded by <s>Oṃ</s>, the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances), beginning with [the hymns of] <s>Madhucchandas</s>.
The hymns, with the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> at the end — that collection is called the Immortal (<s>Amṛta</s>);
the gods formerly attained immortality through this combined [collection].
One who always recites this, purified, attains immortality.
In the middle of this one should insert many ancestral hymns (<s>pitṛsūktas</s>);
one should know that as the ancestral collection — and with it one pleases the ancestors.
Likewise, having collected [the relevant hymns], the <s>Vāsavī</s> collection comes into being;
the <s>Raudra</s>, <s>Ādityā</s>, <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> — whichever deity-collection one desires.
One knowing <s>dharma</s> should perform the <s>vāstu śamana</s> (house-pacification rite) in the middle of the cow-pen.
With flowers, fragrances, garlands, forest products, and herbs,
one should scatter throughout the entire dwelling, and likewise with seven grains.
One should worship <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (Lord of the dwelling) there with a milk-rice [offering], and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;
with <s>audumbara</s> and <s>palāśa</s> [leaves], one should make offerings in each direction.
<s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>,
<s>Soma</s>, great <s>Indra</s> — these are the deities remembered [as presiding] over the directions.
One should give gifts to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> — [then] there is auspiciousness in the dwelling.
This should be done every year in the house by the householder.
If there is anything else of this kind that has not been stated—
regarding <s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and other deities—
whoever, desiring to propitiate, approaches whichever deity,
with an appropriate hymn, as the purpose has been indicated—
through the mantra-vision of the sages, direct accomplishment is to be expected.
Everywhere one should give the ritual fee (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>) or wealth for the success of the rite.
There is indeed no rite without a ritual fee—thus says <s>Śaunaka</s>.
According to one's capacity, even measured by a full vessel at the very least, it should be given.
Therefore, even a small ritual fee must be given for the success of the rite.
One should give eleven bulls, or whatever pleases the preceptor.
To one who knows <s>dharma</s> and speaks truth, the gift of <s>Brahman</s> (sacred knowledge) is given.
This is the supreme, secret, purifying, wondrous <s>Brahman</s>.
It should not be given to one who is not tranquil, nor to one without sons who is devoid of austerity,
nor to one who has not resided with the teacher for a year, nor to a non-student, nor to one who is hostile.
For men bereft of fortune who do not know the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>,
this <s>Ṛgveda</s>, which is a wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpavṛkṣa</s>), does not yield fruit.
The <s>Ṛgveda</s> appears to me like a dwelling containing jewels;
without the lamp of the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, it does not shine forth.
The <s>Ṛgveda</s>, noble like a mine of gems, is extremely difficult to traverse;
without the great vessel of the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, it does not yield fruit.

body.translated_text: The <s>Ṛgveda</s> is the treasury of all jewels, the temple of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.translated_text: Yet this <s>Ṛgveda</s>, when merely recited, becomes fruitless for men.
Therefore, without the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, [the <s>Veda</s>] should be studied with great effort.
He who understands the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, the exposition of the true meaning of the hymns—
for him, by its grace, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> comes alive, with a mind in full bloom.
The practice of the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s> bestows longevity, is the root of prosperity, and destroys all impurity;
it confers the highest radiant fame.
The twice-born who knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s> united with the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>
surely becomes the refuge of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
The first among the <s>Vedas</s>, the lord, the treasury of <s>Āyurveda</s>—
by the constant practice of the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, it becomes exceedingly pleased.
The destruction of enemies, satisfaction of mind, and gatherings of friends—
the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, when gratified by the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, always bestows these.
He who knows the <s>Ṛgveda</s> with all its limbs (<s>sāṅga</s>), always devoted to the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>—
his desires are fulfilled even beyond his wishes.
In lineage, birth, character, wisdom, and also in endeavor—
through the complete knowledge of the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>, they praise the fulfillment of purpose.
All deities are pleased, prosperities are attained,
and incurable afflictions perish for those who constantly recite the <s>Ṛgvidhāna</s>.
As was the manuscript seen, so have I written it.
Whether it is correct or incorrect, no fault is attributed to me.
He who, having copied a sage's work, gives it to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—
his ancestors dwell in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> for as many years as there are syllables.
With broken back, hips, and neck, with clenched fist and face downward—
with such hardship was this written; may it be preserved with care.
Protect it from oil! Protect it from water! Protect it from a loose binding!
Protect it from going into another's hand!—thus speaks the manuscript.
